reason: The PROBLEM is real and verified, but the PROPOSED FIX is wrong in three ways that would make the artifact worse, so the finding is refuted with the corrected fix below. Verified first: lately.html:663 hard-codes LIMITS[1] = "The date recorder switched on in August. History accrues forward only." while the reading line at lately.html:725 renders esc(D.readingLong) from fixture.js -> "Read at 09:14, Thursday 16 July 2026". Driven in chromium at 1440x960, the pair renders together in full, partial, quiet and first-run; the tile carries the label NOT YET over a past-tense verb, and its two siblings are present-tense and self-consistent ("has no callers yet", "keeps no structured decision record"), so tile two is the only one out of voice. The sentence is unresolvable either way: read as August 2026 it is a past tense about a month that has not happened at the stated now; read as August 2025 the refusal falsifies itself, because eleven months of forward-accruing history would exist and the metric would be printable. In first-run it is worse still - "Yours arrive on 10 August" (future) sits on the same screen as "switched on in August" (past), so one of the two must be false. This is the paid-for "unanchored time" / self-contradicting-fact class in lessons.md creeping back, and interaction-check.mjs's own "unanchored time" block does not catch it: it only asserts readingLong is printed at least once, so this is not a restatement of a gate. SEVERITY: defect is right, but it is the top of that class, not the bottom - the untruth is about the product's own provenance rather than about her work, so she is confused rather than misled, but it sits inside the one movement whose entire job is credibility, and it should be fixed this round rather than deferred. WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED. (1) It says to add recordStart to fixture.js. fixture.js is emitted by derive-fixture.mjs and its own header says do not edit; `node derive-fixture.mjs --check` fails on any byte of drift and the next generate overwrites the key. The change belongs in derive-fixture.mjs, not in the generated file. (2) It says to bind recordStart "to the same source" as readingDate. src/lib/project-truth-fixture.ts carries no record-start fact - it exposes PROJECT_TRUTH_TODAY, PROJECT_TRUTH_ACTOR.name, the harbourHouse summary (name, slug, activeRootTaskCount) and rootTaskTitles; the only other instant is CLIFF_WALK_ARCHIVED_AT, an archived-at on a different Project. Declaring a bound derivation for a value the source does not carry is exactly what derive-fixture.mjs's header forbids - "inventing a derivation would be the same defect in better handwriting" - and it would put a fabricated provenance claim inside the honest-degradation contract, a protected object. (3) "rendered through the same formatter as the reading line" is mechanically wrong: readingLong is built in derive-fixture.mjs with a hard-coded "09:14, " prefix, so the tile would read "since 09:14, Monday 6 July 2026" - a clock time stamped on a start date. (4) The invariant is the wrong shape: recordStart <= readingDate is necessary but insufficient, because any earlier start means the recorder IS running and the tile's own ghost plot says the chart stays empty "until the recorder has run for three periods" - so the guard must be a window, not a floor. (5) It leaves the sibling hard-code in first-run untouched, and "10 August" is in fact weeks[11].iso + 28 days (2026-07-13 + 28 = 2026-08-10), i.e. correct only by coincidence and silently wrong the moment PROJECT_TRUTH_TODAY moves.
sharpenedFix: Cheapest correct fix, and the one that matches the tile's own NOT YET label and its two siblings' present tense: drop the month entirely and state the condition, adding no data and no gate - LIMITS[1] becomes "Nothing has recorded a date move yet. History accrues forward only, from the day it starts." If a start date is genuinely wanted, do it honestly: declare recordStart in derive-fixture.mjs (never by hand in fixture.js), place it in labAuthored alongside weeklyCompletions/jobAges/statusCounts because the bound source has no such fact, derive it from readingDate rather than typing a month, render it with a date-only formatter split out of the readingLong builder (drop the "09:14, " prefix), and guard it with a window not a floor - fail the build unless recordStart <= readingDate AND readingDate - recordStart < 21 days, so the refusal cannot falsify itself against the ghost plot's "three periods". In the same change, derive the first-run line from weeks[11].iso + 28 days instead of the literal "10 August", and close the class in interaction-check.mjs with an assertion that no literal month name appears in surface copy unless it was produced by the fixture formatter - that single assertion catches both hard-codes and any future one.
breaks: Low blast radius, but three things to re-measure. (a) Copy length changes the third limit tile's line count; the three tiles are a row that must stay balanced, so re-shoot and re-check the limits band at 390, 768, 1280 and 1440 - the sharpened wording is close to the current length, the seat's "since 09:14, Monday 6 July 2026" was not. (b) Any edit to derive-fixture.mjs must be followed by `node derive-fixture.mjs` and then `node derive-fixture.mjs --check`, or the drift gate fails on a stale fixture.js; the new labAuthored key must also be reflected on the surface's provenance line, which already names lab-authored values. (c) Re-run audit.mjs (leading and type-ramp only, no palette or contrast surface changes) and interaction-check.mjs, including the added month-name assertion, then re-capture all ten frames plus the first-run frame, because that state renders both changed strings. The new build-time window guard will fire if PROJECT_TRUTH_TODAY ever moves more than three weeks past a fixed recordStart - which is the point, but it means the guard must be derived from readingDate rather than pinned, or the lab breaks on the next fixture bump.
